title: Open model gating clauses and contract specification for catalog entry
creator: Luca Ortega
description: Clarify and formalize the admission contract and gating clauses for new open models submitted to the Redwood model catalog. The goal is to define a repeatable, automated, and human-reviewable set of requirements that covers legal/provenance checks, runtime compatibility signals, performance and cost baselines, and a graduated certification path (staging -> verified -> certified). This PRD captures acceptance criteria, non-go scope, required artifacts for intake, and the trade-offs between speed-to-admit and safety/operational cost.
background: We currently accept many community model submissions with ad-hoc checks resulting in inconsistent runtime failures and occasional regressions in cost/latency. Recent incidents (see incident notes) showed KV cache incompatibilities and quantized kernel regressions for two community variants that caused customer-facing latency spikes. Product needs a clearer admission contract that balances rapid adoption of open models with predictable serving economics and safety.
scope_changes: Initial proposal (v0) focused on license & provenance only. Based on runtime and ENG feedback we expanded scope to include: 1) automated perf profiling (latency/tokens/sec on representative instances), 2) a lightweight quantization smoke-test, 3) explicit runtime capability flags (kv_cache_ok, streaming_safe, mixed_precision_tolerant), and 4) a staged rollout requirement (staging -> canary -> certified) with rollback hooks. These additions increase intake friction but reduce production incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Submitter provides: license text (OSI or compatible), SHA256 checksum of weights, model provenance note (training data summary) and pointer to model card or license file.
Automated compatibility tests execute on merge: kernel-compat smoke test, quantization-compat smoke test, and prefix/KV cache sanity check with representative prompts.

Performance baseline: model must meet documented latency and throughput thresholds within 30% of expected family baseline on at least one supported runtime profile (e.g., 8k context on A100-80GB class). Failure requires explicit opt-in for degraded-tier serving.

Safety/Domains: For models that include generation components, submitter must provide an evaluation report for the standard Redwood safety suite (toxicity & safety classifiers). Models failing threshold are flagged for human review and cannot be certified.

Rollout policy: new models enter 'staging' with traffic cap 1% and a 48-hour monitoring window; automatic promotion to 'verified' if no critical regressions and cost delta < 20% over baseline; manual review required for 'certified' status.
Operational artifacts: a linked GitHub PR with CI logs, a perf dashboard snapshot (Grafana link), and a conformance checklist populated in the intake form.
Documented fallback mapping: if a model is marked incompatible for a given runtime, the catalog must surface a compatible fallback variant and a rationale message for routing policies.

Security review flagged: models that request elevated permissions (private weights, on-prem bundle) must set security_review_required=true and complete an external review before promotion beyond staging.

Backward compatibility: model version updates must provide a compatibility declaration (major/minor semantic) and pass a regression eval suite; automated soft-pin policy applies if regressions exceed thresholds.
Acceptance gate: a product sign-off and an ENG sign-off recorded in the intake ticket are required to mark the catalog entry 'certified'.
non_go_scope: This ticket does not redesign the runtime scheduler or change kernel selection heuristics. It also does not modify Dedicated capacity contract terms. Future work will scope fine-grained autoscaling guardrails for new model families.
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Product + ENG alignment: expand intake beyond legal checks to include perf & runtime smoke tests (Luca O., Maya C., Daniel R.).
2026-03-02: Security require external review only for models requesting on-prem/offline distribution (Security review requirement added) (Aisha K.).
2026-03-09: Agreed rollout caps: 1% initial traffic, 48h monitoring window, promotion rules approved (Sofia P., Ravi N.).
risks: Increased time-to-admit may reduce community submissions; mitigated via a lightweight 'expedited review' path for known authors.
Automated perf tests may give false negatives on uncommon hardware; require documented supported hardware matrix.
Licensing ambiguity for certain weights might require legal escalation delaying admission.
notes_for_engineering: ENG: please implement the three automated smoke-tests as reusable CI steps. Provide a minimal Docker test harness to run quantization smoke test on CI. Expose runtime capability flags as part of catalog metadata. If tests are flaky, add a 'retry once' policy and capture logs in the intake ticket.
next_steps: 1) ENG to prototype CI smoke tests (target: 2026-03-20). 2) Product to finalize intake form fields and UX copy (target: 2026-03-17). 3) Security to confirm review rubric for on-prem requests (target: 2026-03-24).
